title: The world
takeaway: The world looks beautiful, but don't get trapped by it: it's a place you're only passing through.
scene: A short poem about 'dunya', the world, meaning worldly life. The poet admits it is beautiful, and warns that it is also a trap.

original: دنیا کوڑہ مقام ہے راہیاں دا
پھل پھل سوہنے ہیرے لعل دنیا
transliteration: Duniya koorha muqaam hai raahiyaan da
Phal phull sohne heere laal duniya
translation: The world is a false resting place for travellers,
though the world is full of lovely fruit and flowers, diamonds and rubies.
couplets.story: This world is only a stopover on a journey, not our real home. It's full of beautiful things like fruit, flowers and jewels.

original: انج ویکھئے تے نظراں وچ چبھے
transliteration: Inj vekhiye te nazraan vich chubhe
translation: When you look at it, it catches your eye:
how beautiful, how easy, how wonderful the world seems!
couplets.story: When you look at it, it grabs your attention. It seems so beautiful, so easy and so amazing.

original: جہنوں ویکھ لو اوہو پیا روے
تھاں تھاں تے ویکھے وبال دنیا
transliteration: Jihnu vekh lo oho piya rove
Thaan thaan te vekhe vabaal duniya
translation: Yet whoever you look at is crying;
everywhere you look, the world is a burden.
couplets.story: Look closer, though, and everyone is crying about something. Everywhere, the world causes trouble.

original: کسے نوں دلہن وو ہٹی تے رانی لگے
دل کھو لئے حسن جمال دنیا
transliteration: Kise nu dulhan vohti te raani lagge
Dil kho laye husn jamaal duniya
translation: To some it looks like a bride, a wife, a queen;
with its beauty and charm, the world steals hearts.
couplets.story: To some people, the world looks like a beautiful bride or a queen. Its beauty steals their hearts.

original: احمدؔ گھر ایہہ غماں مصیبتاں دا
اصل وچ اے نرا جنجال دنیا
transliteration: Ahmad ghar eh ghamaan museebataan da
Asal vich ae nira janjaal dunya
translation: Ahmad, this is a house of sorrows and troubles:
in truth, the world is nothing but a tangle.
couplets.story: He ends plainly. This world is a house full of sadness and problems. Really, it's just one big tangle.

deeper: This poem sums up a classic Sufi and Islamic teaching. The world (dunya) is a temporary 'stopping place for travellers', not the final home. The Prophet said, 'Be in this world as if you were a stranger or a traveller.' The image of the world as a bride or queen who steals hearts is a famous Sufi warning: worldly attractions can pull the heart away from God. The poet doesn't say the world is ugly. He says don't get stuck in it.
why: It's honest that the world is beautiful and still reminds us not to let it trap us. It's a balanced, grown-up way to think about life.
prompt: What's something you enjoy that could become a 'trap' if you let it take over?
notes: Links to the 'big tangle' (janjaal) image on page 49.
